     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0FiniteStageChartBaseChange
     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# Naturality of affine scalar extension
    10	
    11	For an algebra map A -> B, base change carries Spec B -> Spec A to the
    12	contravariant Spec of the scalar-extended algebra map.  The tensor factors are
    13	ordered with the extension ring on the left, matching the finite-stage Picard
    14	ring comparisons.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	set_option autoImplicit false
    18	
    19	universe u
    20	
    21	open CategoryTheory Limits TensorProduct
    22	open scoped TensorProduct
    23	
    24	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    25	
    26	noncomputable section
    27	
    28	namespace Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
    29	
    30	variable (R K A B : Type u)
    31	variable [CommRing R] [CommRing K] [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    32	variable [Algebra R K] [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B]
    33	
    34	/-- The affine base-change isomorphism with the extension ring as the left
    35	tensor factor. -/
    36	noncomputable def affineBaseChangeIso :
    37	    pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R A)))
    38	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R K))) ≅
    39	      Spec (.of (K ⊗[R] A)) :=
    40	  pullbackSymmetry _ _ ≪≫ pullbackSpecIso R K A
    41	
    42	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
    43	theorem affineBaseChangeIso_inv_fst :
    44	    (affineBaseChangeIso R K A).inv ≫ pullback.fst _ _ =
    45	      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
    46	        (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight :
    47	          A →ₐ[R] K ⊗[R] A).toRingHom) := by
    48	  simp [affineBaseChangeIso]
    49	
    50	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
    51	theorem affineBaseChangeIso_inv_snd :
    52	    (affineBaseChangeIso R K A).inv ≫ pullback.snd _ _ =
    53	      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
    54	        (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom :
    55	          K →+* K ⊗[R] A)) := by
    56	  simp [affineBaseChangeIso]
    57	
    58	/-- Base change of an affine morphism over Spec R. -/
    59	noncomputable def affineBaseChangeMap (phi : A →ₐ[R] B) :
    60	    pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R B)))
    61	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R K))) ⟶
    62	      pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R A)))
    63	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R K))) :=
    64	  pullback.map _ _ _ _
    65	    (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom phi.toRingHom)) (𝟙 _) (𝟙 _)
    66	    (by
    67	      rw [Category.comp_id, ← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
    68	      congr 2
    69	      exact phi.comp_algebraMap.symm)
    70	    (by simp)
    71	
    72	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
    73	theorem affineBaseChangeMap_fst (phi : A →ₐ[R] B) :
    74	    affineBaseChangeMap R K A B phi ≫ pullback.fst _ _ =
    75	      pullback.fst _ _ ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom phi.toRingHom) := by
    76	  unfold affineBaseChangeMap
    77	  exact pullback.lift_fst _ _ _
    78	
    79	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
    80	theorem affineBaseChangeMap_snd (phi : A →ₐ[R] B) :
    81	    affineBaseChangeMap R K A B phi ≫ pullback.snd _ _ =
    82	      pullback.snd _ _ := by
    83	  unfold affineBaseChangeMap
    84	  rw [pullback.lift_snd]
    85	  simp
    86	
    87	set_option maxHeartbeats 12800000 in
    88	-- Both pullback projections expand tensor-product universal maps.
    89	/-- The affine base-change isomorphisms intertwine a base-changed morphism with
    90	the Spec of its scalar extension. -/
    91	theorem affineBaseChangeIso_naturality (phi : A →ₐ[R] B) :
    92	    affineBaseChangeMap R K A B phi ≫ (affineBaseChangeIso R K A).hom =
    93	      (affineBaseChangeIso R K B).hom ≫
    94	        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
    95	          (AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
    96	            (R := R) (K := K) phi).toRingHom) := by
    97	  rw [← cancel_epi (affineBaseChangeIso R K B).inv]
    98	  simp only [Iso.inv_hom_id_assoc]
    99	  rw [← cancel_mono (affineBaseChangeIso R K A).inv]
   100	  simp only [Category.assoc, Iso.hom_inv_id, Category.comp_id]
   101	  apply pullback.hom_ext
   102	  · rw [Category.assoc, affineBaseChangeMap_fst]
   103	    simp only [Category.assoc]
   104	    rw [affineBaseChangeIso_inv_fst_assoc (R := R) (K := K) (A := B)]
   105	    rw [affineBaseChangeIso_inv_fst (R := R) (K := K) (A := A)]
   106	    rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
   107	    rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
   108	    congr 2
   109	  · rw [Category.assoc, affineBaseChangeMap_snd]
   110	    simp only [Category.assoc]
   111	    rw [affineBaseChangeIso_inv_snd (R := R) (K := K) (A := B)]
   112	    rw [affineBaseChangeIso_inv_snd (R := R) (K := K) (A := A)]
   113	    rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
   114	    congr 2
   115	    ext x
   116	    simp [AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom]
   117	
   118	end Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
   119	
   120	end
   121	
   122	end AlgebraicGeometry

    36	set_option maxHeartbeats 12800000 in

    38	restriction is the exact left restriction of the separably closed atlas. -/
    39	theorem restrictionBaseChangeMap_naturality
    40	    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k]

    49	  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic P.M.1 k := by infer_instance
    50	  apply affineBaseChangeIso_trans_naturality
    51	    P.N.1 k
    52	    (P.N.1 ⊗[P.M.1]
    53	      Pic0FiniteStageChartModelRing C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M U)
    54	    (P.N.1 ⊗[P.M.1]
    55	      Pic0FiniteStageOverlapModelRing C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M U V)
    56	    (Pic0FiniteStageRing C (Sum.inl U))
    57	    (Pic0FiniteStageRing C (Sum.inr (U, V)))
    58	    (restrictionBaseChangeAlgHom C P U V)
    59	    (chartFinalBaseChangeEquiv C P U)
    60	    (overlapFinalBaseChangeEquiv C P U V)
    61	    (exactRestrictionAlgHom C U V)
    62	  exact pic0FiniteStageFinalBaseChangeEquiv_naturality
    63	    C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.e P.M P.mapM P.hmapM P.N
    64	      (Sum.inl (Sum.inl (U, V)))
    65

      "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once.      8	
     9	/-!
    10	# The finite-stage Picard gluing diagram after base change
    11	
    12	The chart and overlap comparisons identify the multispan diagram obtained by
    13	base-changing the finite-stage gluing with the canonical diagram of the exact
    14	separably closed atlas.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	set_option autoImplicit false
    18	
    19	universe u
    20	
    21	open CategoryTheory Limits TensorProduct
    22	open scoped TensorProduct
    23	
    24	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    25	
    26	noncomputable section
    27	
    28	/-- The spectrum of an algebra homomorphism lies over the base spectrum. -/
    29	theorem specMap_algHom_comp_algebraMap
    30	    {R A B : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    31	    [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B] (r : A →ₐ[R] B) :
    32	    Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom r.toRingHom) ≫
    33	        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R A)) =
    34	      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R B)) := by
    35	  rw [← Spec.map_comp]
    36	  rw [← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
    37	  congr 1
    38	  ext x
    39	  exact r.commutes x
    40	
    41	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    42	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    43	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [IsSepClosed k]
    44	
    45	namespace Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
    46	
    47	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 3200000 in
    48	-- Raw tensor carriers keep the dependent finite-subextension instances visible.
    49	set_option maxHeartbeats 12800000 in
    50	/-- An overlap in the base-changed finite-stage gluing is the corresponding
    51	overlap in the canonical gluing diagram of the exact Picard atlas. -/
    52	noncomputable def gluingOverlapIso
    53	    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k]
    54	    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F)
    55	    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
    56	    (Scheme.Pullback.gluing P.glueData.openCover P.gluedMap
    57	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.N.1 k)))).V (U, V) ≅
    58	      (pic0SepClosedAtlasGlueData C).V (U, V) := by
    59	  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic P.L.1 k := by infer_instance
    60	  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic P.M.1 k := by infer_instance
    61	  let r :=
    62	    AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
    63	      (R := P.M.1) (K := P.N.1)
    64	        (P.mapM (Sum.inl (Sum.inl (U, V))))
    65	  have hStructure :=
    66	    calc
    67	      P.glueData.f U V ≫ P.glueData.ι U ≫ P.gluedMap =
    68	          Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom r.toRingHom) ≫
    69	            Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.N.1 _)) := by
    70	        rw [glueData_f C P U V, glueData_ι_gluedMap C P U]
    71	        rfl
    72	      _ = _ := specMap_algHom_comp_algebraMap r
    73	  exact
    74	    gluingOverlapFlatteningIso C P U V ≪≫
    75	      pullback.congrHom hStructure rfl ≪≫
    76	      overlapBaseChangeIso C P U V ≪≫
    77	      (isPullback_opens_inf U.1.1 V.1.1).isoPullback
    78	
    79	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 3200000 in
    80	-- Comparing both paths unfolds the package's dependent scalar towers.
    81	set_option maxHeartbeats 12800000 in
    82	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
    83	/-- The overlap comparison commutes with the restriction to its left chart. -/
    84	theorem gluingOverlapIso_fst
    85	    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k]
    86	    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F)
    87	    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
    88	    (Scheme.Pullback.gluing P.glueData.openCover P.gluedMap
    89	          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.N.1 k)))).f U V ≫
    90	        (gluingChartIso C P U).hom =
    91	      (gluingOverlapIso C P U V).hom ≫
    92	        (pic0SepClosedAtlasGlueData C).f U V := by
    93	  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic P.L.1 k := by infer_instance
    94	  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic P.M.1 k := by infer_instance
    95	  let r :=
    96	    AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
    97	      (R := P.M.1) (K := P.N.1)
    98	        (P.mapM (Sum.inl (Sum.inl (U, V))))
    99	  have hStructure :=
   100	    calc
   101	      P.glueData.f U V ≫ P.glueData.ι U ≫ P.gluedMap =
   102	          Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom r.toRingHom) ≫
   103	            Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.N.1 _)) := by
   104	        rw [glueData_f C P U V, glueData_ι_gluedMap C P U]
   105	        rfl
   106	      _ = _ := specMap_algHom_comp_algebraMap r
   107	  have hPullback :
   108	      (Scheme.Pullback.gluing P.glueData.openCover P.gluedMap
   109	            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.N.1 k)))).f U V ≫
   110	          (pullback.congrHom (glueData_ι_gluedMap C P U) rfl).hom =
   111	        (gluingOverlapFlatteningIso C P U V).hom ≫
   112	          (pullback.congrHom hStructure rfl).hom ≫
   113	            restrictionBaseChangeMap C P U V := by
   114	    apply pullback.hom_ext
   115	    all_goals simp only [Category.assoc]
   116	  rw [← cancel_mono U.1.1.ι]
